tracks.title: Problem
tracks.question: Problem
tracks.answer: When organizations adopt RAG-based AI, I do not think the goal should be simply to maximize answer accuracy. In real work, it is risky when users accept weakly supported answers too easily, but it is also a problem when they distrust useful answers and refuse to use them. My interest is therefore not in making people trust AI more, but in helping them verify its outputs and rely on them appropriately.

tracks.title: Personal starting point
tracks.question: Personal starting point
tracks.answer: This research interest comes from three different experiences. At GfK, I saw that the same market data could support very different decisions depending on how it was structured and presented. While running Oosu Saloin, I learned that real operational decisions often depend on tacit knowledge and exceptions that cannot be fully captured in a manual. More recently, while building AskOosu, I found that showing what evidence an AI answer is based on, and revealing when the available information is insufficient, can matter as much as making the answer itself sound natural.

tracks.title: Research question
tracks.question: Research question
tracks.answer: My research question is therefore the following. tracks.answer: 기존 연구는 크게 세 흐름으로 나눠볼 수 있습니다. 첫째, Tom Steinberger 교수님의 연구처럼 도메인 전문가가 실제 업무에서 데이터를 어떻게 해석하고 사용하는지를 다룬 연구가 있습니다. 둘째, 사람이 AI의 설명과 투명성을 어떻게 받아들이고, 언제 AI를 신뢰하거나 의심하는지를 다룬 연구가 있습니다. 셋째, RAG와 대규모 언어모델에서 인용과 출처 추적의 품질을 높이는 기술 연구도 빠르게 발전하고 있습니다. 하지만 조직의 지식구조와 검증 인터페이스를 함께 바꿔가며, 사용자가 실제로 출처를 열고 비교하거나 AI의 답을 수정·거부하는 행동까지 측정한 연구는 아직 충분하지 않다고 봅니다. 저는 이 세 흐름을 실제 조직 업무 안에서 연결하고 싶습니다.

tracks.title: Literature gap
tracks.question: Literature gap
tracks.answer: I see three relevant research streams that have largely developed in parallel. First, CSCW work such as Professor Tom Steinberger's research explains how domain experts interpret and use data in situated work practices. Second, human-AI interaction research examines explanations, transparency, trust, and appropriate reliance. Third, technical RAG research is rapidly improving citation and provenance quality. What remains less clearly connected is how organizational knowledge structure and verification-interface design jointly shape observable behaviors such as opening sources, comparing evidence, revising an answer, or rejecting it during real work. I want to connect these three streams in an organizational task setting.

tracks.title: Argument
tracks.question: Argument
tracks.answer: My basic argument is that simply showing more information will not be enough. Even if provenance or uncertainty is visible, users may not verify the answer if doing so does not fit naturally into their workflow. In contrast, verification controls that let users quickly open original sources or compare the supporting evidence may reduce over-reliance. I also expect these effects to differ depending on domain expertise and time pressure.

tracks.title: Method
tracks.question: Method
tracks.answer: I would like to conduct the study in three main stages. First, I would interview domain experts who use AI in their work to understand when they decide to verify an answer and what information they need in order to do so. Second, based on those findings, I would build a RAG prototype that keeps the underlying knowledge and answers constant while varying factors such as provenance, freshness indicators, or verification controls. Third, I would run a controlled experiment using tasks that resemble real workplace decisions. Rather than relying only on self-reported trust or satisfaction, I would also collect behavioral measures such as whether participants open a source, revise an answer, or reject an incorrect output. I would then compare task accuracy and decision quality to identify which designs support calibrated reliance rather than simply increasing trust. Where possible, I would keep the underlying model output constant so that the experiment isolates the effect of information and interface design.

Rather than relying only on self-reported trust or satisfaction, I would also collect behavioral measures such as whether participants open a source, revise an answer, or reject an incorrect output.
I would then compare task accuracy and decision quality to identify which designs support calibrated reliance rather than simply increasing trust.
Where possible, I would keep the underlying model output constant so that the experiment isolates the effect of information and interface design.

tracks.title: BTM and faculty fit
tracks.question: BTM and faculty fit
tracks.answer: To conduct this study properly, my first priority would be to strengthen the research-design and quantitative skills that I still lack. KAIST BTM's research-methods and digital-innovation courses would provide that foundation. The primary intellectual anchor is Professor Tom Steinberger's work on domain experts, situated data practices, and actionable data science. I want to extend that problem into generative AI and workplace RAG by studying the conditions under which domain experts actually verify and use AI outputs. Professor Hangjung Zo's work on AI transparency, trust, and user responses can provide a complementary lens on how verification information shapes users' reactions, while Professor Hyunju Jung's work on technology search and knowledge recombination offers a higher-level perspective on how organizations combine existing knowledge with external AI capabilities. For the master's thesis itself, however, I would keep the scope focused on domain-expert verification behavior and workflow fit, where the connection to Professor Steinberger's work is strongest.

tracks.answer: The core concern is the same. In my application, I broadly proposed studying how source transparency, error handling, and workflow fit influence trust and continuance intention. tracks.title: What is the gap in the existing literature?
tracks.question: What is the gap in the existing literature?
tracks.answer: There is extensive research on explainability, transparency, trust, and technology adoption. However, many studies measure trust or intention through self-reports, or examine interface features separately from the organizational knowledge structure behind them. In workplace RAG systems, what is retrieved and presented as authoritative knowledge is determined at the same time as who is expected to verify it and how. I want to study how knowledge structures and verification interfaces lead to calibrated reliance through observable behaviors such as source opening, cross-checking, accepting correct answers, and rejecting incorrect answers. I would not claim that no one has studied this; I would use a systematic literature review to establish the relative gap more precisely.

tracks.title: What is your central argument or hypothesis?
tracks.question: What is your central argument or hypothesis?
tracks.answer: My central argument is that transparency does not automatically increase appropriate trust. It produces calibrated reliance only when users can act on the information through meaningful verification controls. Showing more source and freshness information may even create cognitive burden. In contrast, when original-source access, follow-up questioning, uncertainty cues, correction, and approval are integrated into the workflow, users are more likely to accept sound answers and inspect questionable ones. I also expect these effects to vary by domain expertise and time pressure.

tracks.question: 왜 신뢰가 아니라 ‘적정 의존’을 보려 합니까?

tracks.title: Why study calibrated reliance rather than trust?
tracks.question: Why study calibrated reliance rather than trust?
tracks.answer: Increasing trust without qualification can be dangerous. If users trust incorrect answers, automation bias and overreliance can result. The desired outcome is not that users believe the AI more, but that they efficiently use correct answers and inspect or reject answers that are incorrect or weakly supported. I would therefore measure trust and continuance intention as secondary outcomes, while using acceptance of correct answers, rejection of incorrect answers, source-checking behavior, and final decision quality as the central outcomes.

tracks.answer: 두 단계의 혼합연구를 생각하고 있습니다. 먼저 지식노동자나 도메인 실무자를 인터뷰해서 실제로 어떤 상황에서 AI의 답을 다시 확인하는지 파악하겠습니다. 그 결과를 바탕으로 출처와 최신성을 얼마나 쉽게 확인할 수 있는지, 그리고 원문 확인이나 수정 기능을 어느 정도 제공할지를 달리한 RAG 프로토타입을 만들고 통제실험을 진행하겠습니다. 필요한 표본 수는 실험설계를 정한 뒤 통계적으로 계산하고, 설문뿐 아니라 출처 클릭, 검토시간, 오답 거부율과 최종 과업성과 같은 행동 데이터를 핵심 자료로 보겠습니다.

tracks.title: How would you design the methodology?
tracks.question: How would you design the methodology?
tracks.answer: I am considering a two-stage mixed-method design. First, I would interview approximately eight to twelve knowledge workers or domain practitioners to understand their actual verification routines and exception-handling practices. Based on those findings, I would build RAG prototypes that vary the visibility of source and freshness information and the level of verification control. I would determine the sample size through an a priori power analysis and combine online participants with practitioner networks where feasible. Surveys would measure perceived information quality, trust, and cognitive load, while behavioral logs such as source clicks, review time, rejection of incorrect answers, and final task performance would be the primary data.

tracks.title: What are your independent and dependent variables?
tracks.question: What are your independent and dependent variables?
tracks.answer: The first independent variable would be how clearly source provenance, freshness, and uncertainty are presented. The second would be the level of verification control, such as opening the original source, asking follow-up questions, correcting the output, or requiring approval. Perceived information quality, trust, cognitive load, and continuance intention could be examined as mediators or secondary outcomes.

tracks.question: How would you recruit participants?
tracks.answer: I do not currently have confirmed participation from a specific company. If I begin only with rare, highly specialized experts, the study may become infeasible for a master's thesis. For exploratory interviews, I would approach knowledge workers and small-business practitioners through my professional and entrepreneurial networks. For the experiment, I would consider an online panel with relevant job-experience screening. After admission, I would narrow the work context based on feasibility, and if an organizational partner becomes available, I would use that opportunity to strengthen field validity.

tracks.title: What would you do if the results contradict your expectations?
tracks.question: What would you do if the results contradict your expectations?
tracks.answer: If source information does not increase verification or even reduces performance, I would not regard the study as a failure. I would examine whether the interface created excessive cognitive burden, whether participants lacked the ability to assess source quality, or whether time pressure discouraged checking. The goal is not to confirm that transparency is always beneficial, but to explain the conditions under which it helps, has no effect, or becomes counterproductive.

tracks.title: Is TAM too old and simplistic for this study?
tracks.question: Is TAM too old and simplistic for this study?
tracks.answer: I agree that TAM alone would be insufficient. In my application, I used TAM and trust theory as starting points, but perceived usefulness and ease of use do not adequately explain verification behavior or overreliance. In the final study, I would use TAM only as a baseline for adoption and integrate research on trust in automation, calibrated reliance, human-AI collaboration, organizational routines, and knowledge representation. I would also avoid relying only on self-reported intention by collecting behavioral logs and task-performance measures.

tracks.title: What is the academic contribution of your research?
tracks.question: What is the academic contribution of your research?
tracks.answer: First, the study could interpret metadata, source provenance, and freshness design in RAG not as neutral technical infrastructure, but as mechanisms that shape what an organization recognizes as knowledge and where users direct their attention. tracks.question: What is the practical contribution?
tracks.answer: Small and medium-sized firms often cannot maintain a separate team for AI verification, so the product itself must make clear who should check what and when. These principles could reduce both the cost and risk of organizational AI adoption.

tracks.title: If model accuracy improves, will the trust problem not resolve itself?
tracks.question: If model accuracy improves, will the trust problem not resolve itself?
tracks.answer: Higher accuracy is a necessary foundation, but it is not sufficient. Organizational knowledge continues to change, and the same answer may be usable or unusable depending on the authority and freshness of its source. A highly accurate model can also increase the risk of uncritical reliance because users become less likely to check it. Therefore, performance improvement must be accompanied by designs that let users inspect evidence and limitations and that define who approves and takes responsibility for the output.

tracks.question: Are you forcing a connection between your interests and the professors' research?
tracks.answer: The connection is not based only on the shared use of the term AI. 그래서 ‘내가 경영할 대상과 내가 축적할 전문성은 무엇인가’라는 고민이 오래 지속됐습니다.
이후 GfK의 데이터 업무와 사업 운영을 거쳐 프로그래밍과 RAG 서비스를 직접 구현하면서 기술과 AI가 제가 오래 찾던 구체적 대상이라는 것을 발견했습니다.

기술경영은 기술의 구조, 조직의 업무방식, 사용자의 수용, 시장가치를 함께 다루기 때문에 제 경영 경험과 기술 역량을 가장 일관되게 통합할 수 있는 분야라고 생각합니다.

tracks.title: Why do you want to study technology management?
tracks.question: Why do you want to study technology management?
tracks.answer: As an undergraduate, I learned tools from strategy, marketing, and statistics, but I did not yet have a specific technology or industry problem to which I wanted to apply them deeply. I therefore spent a long time asking what I wanted to manage and what kind of expertise I could build. After working with market data, operating a business, and building RAG services, I realized that technology and AI were the concrete domain I had been looking for. At the same time, I became more interested in why a technology becomes embedded in one organization but fails in another than in development alone. Technology management allows me to study the technical system, organizational workflow, user adoption, and market value together, so it is the field that most coherently integrates my background.

tracks.question: Why did you apply to KAIST BTM?
tracks.answer: What I need is not another broad overview of management, but training that can turn questions from practice into testable research. My main reason for applying is this research and curriculum fit rather than the university's reputation alone.

tracks.title: Why a research-oriented BTM program rather than another MOT program or an MBA?
tracks.question: Why a research-oriented BTM program rather than another MOT program or an MBA?
tracks.answer: I have already experienced market analysis, business operations, and product planning in practice. tracks.title: 왜 지금 대학원에 오려 합니까?
tracks.question: 왜 지금 대학원에 오려 합니까?

tracks.title: Why do you want to enter graduate school now?
tracks.question: Why do you want to enter graduate school now?
tracks.answer: Throughout university and my early career, I kept asking in which field I could develop expertise that would be difficult to replace. Market-data analysis and business operations each left me on one side of the divide between analysis and implementation. When I began programming and building RAG services, I realized that I could connect management, data, and user experience within one technical system. However, experience with one service cannot tell me whether the same mechanism applies to other organizations or which factor is actually causal. My interests have now converged on organizational AI, and I can also build experimental prototypes. That makes this the right time to transform my practical intuition into a research question and receive systematic methodological training.

tracks.title: What does technology management mean to you?
tracks.question: What does technology management mean to you?
tracks.answer: I view technology management not as the study of technical excellence alone, but as the study of how organizations select a technology, place it within workflows, and convert it into value that users and markets can accept. Its core task is to design and evaluate the links among technology, organization, users, and markets, including both performance and unintended consequences. In my proposed research, the key connection is how the technical structure of a RAG system changes organizational attention, verification responsibility, and decision-making.

tracks.title: Why BTM rather than an AI or computer-science program?
tracks.question: Why BTM rather than an AI or computer-science program?
tracks.answer: I have been comfortable learning technology for a long time, and more recently I have confirmed that I can learn Python and RAG systems and turn them into working outputs. However, my central question is not how to build a better foundation model. It is what an organization recognizes as valid knowledge, who verifies an AI answer, and how work and responsibility change after adoption. Even with the same model, organizational judgment can change depending on how document authority and freshness are structured and how verification controls are designed. Development allows me to understand the system realistically and build research prototypes, but the central unit of analysis is the organization and its users. That is why BTM is the better fit.

tracks.title: Why not enter the workforce immediately?
tracks.question: Why not enter the workforce immediately?
tracks.answer: I am not applying to graduate school to postpone employment. If I enter a company immediately, I will have to solve problems within one product's schedule and performance metrics. With training in research methods and empirical analysis, I would be able to design AI product, solution, or transformation strategies based not only on intuition, but on evidence about workflow fit, user verification, and organizational outcomes.

tracks.question: 경력이 너무 산만한 것 아닙니까?
tracks.answer: 직무명만 보면 산만해 보일 수 있습니다. 저 역시 오랫동안 ‘경영학을 어디에 적용해야 나만의 전문성이 되는가’를 고민했습니다. 그러나 각 단계는 무관한 이동이 아니라 이전 단계의 한계를 보완한 과정입니다. GfK에서 시장을 데이터로 읽었지만 실행의 주체성이 부족해 사업을 운영했고, 우수살롱에서 고객과 운영을 직접 다뤘지만 오프라인의 확장성 한계를 경험해 디지털 제품과 개발을 배웠습니다. 프로그래밍과 RAG를 배우면서 데이터·운영·사용자 경험이 하나의 시스템 안에서 연결됐고, 지금은 이 경험을 조직 AI가 실제 업무에서 작동하는 조건이라는 하나의 연구질문으로 통합하고 있습니다.

tracks.title: Is your career path too scattered?
tracks.question: Is your career path too scattered?
tracks.answer: The job titles can look scattered. I also spent a long time asking where management knowledge could become a distinctive specialization for me. However, these were not unrelated moves. At GfK, I learned to read markets through data, but I wanted more responsibility for implementation, so I operated a business. At Oosu Saloin, I worked directly with customers and operations, but I experienced the scalability limits of an offline business, which led me to digital products and development. Programming and RAG then brought data, operations, and user experience together within one system. I am now integrating these experiences into one research question: under what conditions does organizational AI actually work in practice?

tracks.title: How does your GfK experience contribute to your research?
tracks.question: How does your GfK experience contribute to your research?
tracks.answer: At GfK, I organized point-of-sales data by country, channel, and product and transformed it into reports. I learned that a large amount of data does not automatically create insight. The categories and metrics used to structure the data, and the decision-maker for whom it is interpreted, determine its meaning. This directly connects to my RAG question: which documents are treated as retrievable knowledge, and how metadata and freshness are represented, can change both the AI response and the organization's judgment.

tracks.title: What does operating Oosu Saloin have to do with academic research?
tracks.question: What does operating Oosu Saloin have to do with academic research?
tracks.answer: At Oosu Saloin, I designed not only products and marketing, but also ordering, inventory, customer service, employee handoffs, and exception handling. Even when the same manual was available, experienced and new staff interpreted situations differently, and small differences in work sequence and handoffs changed service quality. That experience led me to believe that collecting documents and placing them in an AI system is not enough. The system must also reflect work context and define who is responsible for verification.

tracks.title: What did you learn from closing your business?
tracks.question: What did you learn from closing your business?
tracks.answer: I do not want to present the closure itself as a success. However, for nearly five years I was responsible for real revenue, customers, and operating problems and learned what it takes to keep a small brand functioning. I also learned that an offline business dependent on location, time, and individual labor has clear limits to scale. When tacit knowledge is concentrated in the founder, it is difficult to create a repeatable and transferable system. Those limitations directly motivated me to study digital products and organizational knowledge systems.

tracks.question: GfK·JW CRONY·태영테크처럼 일부 경력이 짧은 이유는 무엇입니까?
tracks.answer: 기간이 짧았던 이유는 각 단계마다 분명한 전환 계기가 있었기 때문입니다. GfK에서는 회사 사정도 좋지 않았고, 담당 고객의 요구에 따라 시장 정의나 데이터 가공 방식이 달라지는 일을 반복해서 보면서 데이터가 항상 중립적인 사실로만 쓰이는 것은 아니라는 점을 크게 느꼈습니다. 그래서 좀 더 실행에 가까운 일을 경험하고 싶어 JW CRONY로 옮겼습니다. 그런데 JW에서는 급여가 몇 달 밀릴 정도로 회사의 안정성이 낮았습니다. 회사원으로서도 큰 불확실성을 감수해야 한다면 차라리 그 리스크를 직접 지고 제 사업을 해보자는 생각으로 이어졌고, 이후 우수살롱 창업을 선택했습니다. 태영테크는 그 이후 제한된 기간의 실무 지원 성격이었습니다.

tracks.title: Why were several of your earlier roles relatively short?
tracks.question: Why were several of your earlier roles relatively short?
tracks.answer: Each short role had a specific reason for transition. At GfK, the company was also going through a difficult period, and I repeatedly saw that market definitions or data framing could change depending on what a client wanted to demonstrate. That experience challenged my earlier belief that data is automatically neutral and made me want to work closer to execution. I therefore moved to JW CRONY. At JW, however, salaries were delayed for several months, so I did not experience the stability I had expected from employment. I began to think that if I had to accept that level of uncertainty anyway, I would rather take the risk directly and build my own business. That thinking led to Oosu Saloin. Taeyoung Tech later had a more limited, short-term support nature.

tracks.answer: 2022년 초 태영테크에서 운영 데이터 분석가로 짧게 근무하면서 수주·매출 관련 사무 데이터를 정리하고 업무 흐름을 개선하는 일을 맡았습니다. 지원서에 기재한 범위에서 말씀드리면, Excel과 Google Sheets를 이용해 흩어진 자료를 정리하고 취합·공유가 더 수월하도록 기본 구조를 만드는 역할이었습니다. 제가 회사의 전략이나 시스템 구축을 총괄한 것은 아니고, 기존 데이터를 실무자가 확인하고 활용하기 쉬운 형태로 정리하는 실무 지원에 가까웠습니다. 이 경험을 통해 작은 데이터 정리와 자동화도 현장의 업무방식을 바꿀 수 있다는 점을 배웠습니다.

tracks.title: What is your greatest strength?
tracks.question: What is your greatest strength?
tracks.answer: My greatest strength is learning new technology quickly and connecting problems from different domains to concrete outputs. The tendency that led me to solve computer problems and adopt new collaboration tools early has now developed into the ability to learn Python and RAG systems and implement them within a relatively short period. At GfK, I translated market questions into data. At Oosu Saloin, I translated customer needs into operating standards. More recently, I translated organizational information and user questions into RAG services and interfaces. In research, I want to use this ability to turn field problems into variables, prototypes, and data rather than leaving them as abstract claims.

tracks.question: Are you applying to graduate school simply to remove the label of being a non-major?

I want to demonstrate my specialization through research outcomes and real problem-solving ability, not merely through a different degree title.

tracks.title: Which undergraduate course was most memorable to you?
tracks.question: Which undergraduate course was most memorable to you?
tracks.answer: The most memorable course was Technology Management and Operations Strategy in the spring of 2018. We studied patterns of innovation, standards competition and market entry, innovation-project selection, new-product development, and technology commercialization. What stayed with me was that possessing a good technology is different from turning it into organizational, operational, and market performance. I received an A+ in the course, and later encountered the same problem through GfK data analysis, Oosu Saloin operations, and AI-service implementation.

tracks.title: How does your management major help your BTM research?
tracks.question: How does your management major help your BTM research?
tracks.answer: As an undergraduate, I learned tools from strategy, marketing, and statistics, but I did not yet have a specific company or technological domain in which I wanted to apply them deeply, so my engagement was inconsistent. Nevertheless, management gave me a framework for viewing technology not merely as a function, but within consumer choice, organizational execution, corporate strategy, and performance. Through later experience in data work, business operations, and programming, I found the concrete domain of AI and organizational knowledge. The management concepts that once felt dispersed then became useful tools for explaining real problems. In graduate school, I want to narrow that breadth into a clear specialization through research methods and organizational-AI research.

tracks.title: 마케팅학회와 공모전 경험이 현재와 어떻게 연결됩니까?
tracks.question: 마케팅학회와 공모전 경험이 현재와 어떻게 연결됩니까?
tracks.answer: 2012년 3월부터 2014년 2월까지 경영학과 마케팅학회 MiFE에서 스태프로 활동하며 매주 사례연구와 토론 미팅을 운영하고 기업연계 프로그램을 경험했습니다. LG전자 스타일러 IMC 학술제에서는 팀으로 전략을 제안해 최우수상을 받았습니다. 당시에는 기술제품의 기능을 소비자가 이해하는 메시지와 시장가치로 바꾸는 문제를 처음 다뤘습니다. 이후 사업 운영과 AI 서비스 구현을 경험하면서 관심이 메시지 전달을 넘어 ‘사용자가 시스템의 답을 어떻게 이해하고 검증해 실제 행동으로 옮기는가’로 깊어졌습니다. 현재 연구는 그 초기 관심을 조직의 검증 행동과 적정 의존으로 확장한 것입니다.

tracks.title: How are your marketing-society and competition experiences connected to your current research?
tracks.question: How are your marketing-society and competition experiences connected to your current research?
tracks.answer: From March 2012 to February 2014, I served as a staff member in the business-school marketing society MiFE, helping run weekly case-study and discussion meetings and participating in industry-linked programs. In an LG Styler IMC project, our team proposed a strategy and received the top award. That experience first exposed me to the problem of translating a technological product's functions into user meaning and market value. After operating a business and building AI services, my interest developed from message delivery to how users interpret, verify, and act on a system's output. My current research extends that early interest into organizational verification behavior and calibrated reliance.

tracks.answer: 3.08은 제 지원서의 가장 분명한 약점이며 변명하지 않겠습니다. 학부 당시 학생회와 학회·공모전 등 여러 활동에 에너지를 배분했고, 경영학의 수단을 어떤 전문영역에 적용할지 목표도 명확하지 않았습니다. 그러나 활동이 많았다는 사실이나 목표가 늦게 정해졌다는 점은 낮은 학점의 면책 사유가 아닙니다. 학업을 기본축으로 두고 우선순위를 조절하지 못한 결과까지 제 책임입니다. 이후 경영통계학 A0, 기술경영 및 운영전략 A+, 마케팅리서치 B+를 받았고, GfK 데이터 업무와 약 5년의 사업 운영, Python·RAG 프로젝트를 지속적으로 완수하면서 시간과 산출물을 관리하는 방식을 바꿨습니다. 입학 전에는 확률통계·회귀분석을 복습하고 관심 논문의 분석을 재현해, 대학원 수학능력을 말이 아니라 결과물로 증명하겠습니다.

tracks.title: Your GPA is 3.08. Can you handle graduate-level coursework?
tracks.question: Your GPA is 3.08. Can you handle graduate-level coursework?
tracks.answer: A GPA of 3.08 is the clearest weakness in my application, and I do not want to make excuses for it. As an undergraduate, I divided my energy among student-government work, an academic society, and competitions, and I did not yet have a clear professional domain in which to apply management knowledge. However, neither the number of activities nor the fact that my direction developed later excuses the GPA. I was responsible for failing to make academics the central priority. Later, I earned an A in Business Statistics, an A+ in Technology Management and Operations Strategy, and a B+ in Marketing Research. I also learned to manage time and outputs through market-data work at GfK, nearly five years of business operations, and sustained Python and RAG projects. Before admission, I will review probability, statistics, and regression and replicate analyses from relevant papers so that my readiness is demonstrated through outputs rather than promises.

tracks.title: 학부 초반 F와 낮은 성적이 많은 이유는 무엇입니까?
tracks.question: 학부 초반 F와 낮은 성적이 많은 이유는 무엇입니까?
tracks.answer:
학부 초반에는 진로 목표가 분명하지 않았고 학생회와 여러 교과 밖 활동까지 벌이면서 수강과 학업을 책임 있게 관리하지 못했습니다. 경영학의 여러 도구를 배우면서도 제가 깊이 파고들 기술이나 산업의 대상을 찾지 못해 몰입도가 낮았던 것도 사실입니다. 그러나 그것은 당시의 상태에 대한 설명이지 성적에 대한 변명이 아닙니다. 우선순위를 조절하지 못한 책임은 제게 있습니다. 이후 관심 과목에서 성과를 내고, 졸업 후에는 데이터 업무와 장기 사업 운영, 개발 프로젝트를 통해 마감과 산출물을 역산해 관리하는 습관을 만들었습니다. 대학원에서는 학기 목표를 주간 단위의 문헌표·분석 재현·연구노트로 쪼개고 스스로 진척을 기록해 같은 문제가 반복되지 않도록 하겠습니다.

실제 개인 사유를 교수에게 설명해야 할 경우에만 사실대로 한 문장을 추가한다. 현재 자료에 없는 이유를 새로 만들지 않는다.

tracks.title: Why did you receive failing and low grades early in college?
tracks.question: Why did you receive failing and low grades early in college?
tracks.answer: Early in college, I did not have a clear career goal and took on student-government and other extracurricular activities without managing my courses responsibly. It is also true that, while learning various management tools, I had not found a technology or industry problem in which I wanted to immerse myself. That explains my state at the time, but it does not excuse the grades. I was responsible for failing to set priorities. Later, I performed better in subjects connected to my interests and developed the habit of planning backward from deadlines and deliverables through data work, long-term business operations, and development projects. In graduate school, I will divide semester goals into weekly literature matrices, replication tasks, and research notes and track my own progress so that the same problem is not repeated.

tracks.question: 논문이나 학부연구 경험이 없는데 연구를 할 준비가 됐습니까?
tracks.answer: 학술논문이나 학부연구 경험이 없다는 점은 분명한 약점입니다. 그래서 제가 이미 연구자라고 주장하기보다 연구훈련을 받아야 하는 지원자라고 생각합니다. 다만 GfK에서 데이터를 구조화하고, 5년간 사업의 운영 문제를 관찰하고, AskOosu에서 출처와 fallback을 직접 구현하면서 연구할 현상과 프로토타입 제작 능력은 확보했습니다. 입학 후에는 연구방법론 수업, 선행연구 매트릭스 작성, 공개 데이터나 논문의 분석 재현부터 시작해 문제의식을 검증 가능한 설계로 바꾸겠습니다.

tracks.title: You have no publication or undergraduate research experience. Are you ready to conduct research?
tracks.question: You have no publication or undergraduate research experience. Are you ready to conduct research?
tracks.answer: The lack of a publication or undergraduate research experience is a clear weakness. I would not claim that I am already a trained researcher; I am applying because I need research training. However, I have developed useful starting assets: structuring market data at GfK, observing operational problems for nearly five years, and directly implementing source links and fallback behavior in AskOosu. These experiences give me a concrete phenomenon to study and the ability to build a prototype. I would begin with research-method courses, a structured literature matrix, and replication of analyses using public data or published papers, and then convert the practical concern into a testable design.

tracks.title: If you could not immerse yourself in management as an undergraduate, how do we know you will not search for another field again?
tracks.question: If you could not immerse yourself in management as an undergraduate, how do we know you will not search for another field again?
tracks.answer: It is true that I did not find a central direction as an undergraduate, and that is reflected in my grades. However, I am no longer exploring a new field in the abstract. At GfK, I experienced data structures and decision-making. During nearly five years of business operations, I dealt with tacit knowledge and exceptions. More recently, I implemented RAG systems. These three experiences have converged on one phenomenon: how organizations structure knowledge and how users verify AI answers. I have specified research questions, variables, and a feasible experimental approach, so my current state of focus is different from the lack of direction I had as an undergraduate.

tracks.question: Why did your undergraduate study span from 2012 to 2018?
tracks.answer: I entered university in 2012 and, after being accepted into KATUSA, took one semester of leave before enlistment. After returning, I completed the credits required for graduation but deferred graduation while looking for work. I later applied to graduate and completed the degree in August 2018. I explain the length of enrollment through this academic timeline, while treating my GPA management as a separate issue for which I take responsibility.

tracks.question: Why did you minor in advertising, PR and branding, and how does it connect to your research now?

The connection is retrospective: through MiFE, the Styler project, and later business operations, my interest in user perception and technology adoption gradually developed into my current research question.

tracks.question: Your professional development experience is short. Can you still conduct RAG research?
tracks.answer: It is correct that my formal development experience is not long. However, my interest in technology did not begin with the recent generative-AI trend. Since childhood, I have replaced computer components, solved software problems, and learned new tools quickly. More recently, I converted that orientation into structured learning and actual outputs by studying Python, backend development, and RAG. In AskOosu, I implemented retrieval, source links, and behavior for insufficient information, and in CodeMap I contributed to problem definition and UX implementation. I do not claim to be a large-model researcher. My role is to understand the system realistically, build research prototypes, and study how technical choices affect organizational behavior and adoption.

tracks.title: Briefly explain the difference between RAG and fine-tuning.
tracks.question: Briefly explain the difference between RAG and fine-tuning.
tracks.answer: RAG retrieves external documents relevant to a question and provides them as context for generation. It is useful when knowledge changes frequently and when source traceability and organization-specific information matter. Fine-tuning uses training data to adjust the model parameters themselves for a task, domain, or response style. Because organizational knowledge changes and requires access control and provenance, RAG is particularly relevant to my research. However, retrieval quality, document structure, permissions, and verification interfaces must be designed together.

tracks.title: What was the most important problem you discovered while building AskOosu?
tracks.question: What was the most important problem you discovered while building AskOosu?
tracks.answer: The most important moment was when AskOosu produced a fluent and plausible answer using outdated or insufficient evidence. I realized that making the sentence more natural was less important than showing which documents had been used and refusing to invent an answer when the information was missing. The system needed to ask a follow-up question or disclose its limitation. That experience led me to treat source provenance, freshness, fallback behavior, and verification roles as potential research variables.

tracks.question: What exactly was your role in CodeMap?
tracks.answer: CodeMap was a team project designed to help users understand an unfamiliar codebase. tracks.title: You wrote that small-business owners may distrust digital tools. What concrete example did you observe?
tracks.question: You wrote that small-business owners may distrust digital tools. What concrete example did you observe?
tracks.answer: When I first opened Oosu Saloin, I received a flood of offers for blog-review campaigns and digital marketing partnerships through Naver messages, text messages, phone calls, and Instagram DMs. The problem was that the sales pitch could sound convincing while the actual service quality or follow-up was often poor, so I became cautious about trusting outside services from the beginning. I had a similar experience with tax services: I changed accountants twice before settling on one recommended by another business owner. This taught me that for small businesses, trust often depends less on the existence of features and more on having credible evidence and a reliable way to verify the provider's actual quality.

tracks.question: What is your greatest weakness?
tracks.answer: When I discover a new problem, I tend to expand quickly into related areas, so the initial scope can become too broad. I now keep the core research question in one sentence and first ask whether a new interest is directly necessary for the literature, variables, or prototype. I define the literature matrix, analysis, or implementation output that must be completed each week and record my progress, which helps me control scope and priorities independently.

tracks.title: What was your most difficult experience, and how did you overcome it?
tracks.question: What was your most difficult experience, and how did you overcome it?
tracks.answer: The most difficult period was operating Oosu Saloin while being responsible at the same time for fluctuating sales, customer service, inventory, and staffing issues. At first, I tried to solve every problem through more personal effort, but that was not sustainable. I began separating and recording sales, products, and operations by time period, and I adjusted customer interactions and work procedures in smaller units. Not every problem was solved, but I learned how to divide an uncertain situation into measurable components and improve them iteratively rather than responding only emotionally.

tracks.title: Tell us about a failure.
tracks.question: Tell us about a failure.
tracks.answer: While operating Oosu Saloin, I personally handled many judgments and exceptional cases. tracks.title: How do you resolve conflict within a team?
tracks.question: How do you resolve conflict within a team?
tracks.answer: When opinions conflict, I first separate the objectives that each option is trying to optimize. For example, if visual completeness conflicts with the development schedule, I do not begin by deciding whose preference is correct. I compare the options against the core user task, the deadline, and the technical debt they create. When possible, I use a small prototype or user feedback as evidence. If an immediate decision is impossible, I record the assumption and set a clear point for reevaluation.

tracks.title: Can you continue when research becomes repetitive and results are slow?
tracks.question: Can you continue when research becomes repetitive and results are slow?
tracks.answer: Operating Oosu Saloin for nearly five years taught me that results come from repeated management and improvement rather than short-term excitement. In development projects, I also revised retrieval, source links, and error handling repeatedly. I do not claim that this means I already know how to conduct academic research well. Research requires even more patience in literature review, data cleaning, and interpreting results that oppose the original expectation. I would maintain consistency through weekly outputs, research notes, and self-monitored progress.

tracks.question: How do you think your recommender, the CEO of Sticks & Stones, would describe you?
tracks.answer: Based on how we worked together, I think my recommender would describe me as someone who looks at business goals and users before the technology itself. During the website redesign, I did not start by choosing a framework; I first clarified what customers needed to find and what the brand needed to communicate. I then investigated the poorly documented WordPress structure, learned the necessary technology, and helped move the site to a TypeScript-based environment. He directly observed that I learn unfamiliar areas independently while considering brand communication, maintenance cost, and operational efficiency together with the technical decision.
